title: Never write an operator identity into a record committed to the target repo
description:
From the ticks pwp run, 2026-09-15.

`ticfac settle --release "<who>"` records the string verbatim as released_by in .ticfac/runs/<run>/decisions/<n>.json, which ticfac COMMITS to the target repository's epic branch. In ticks — a public repository whose rules forbid operator identifiers in tracked files — that failed the public-repo guard and blocked the epic's PR.

Two things to fix:

1. An operator identity handed to a ticfac command must not land verbatim in a committed record. Either take a non-identifying handle, or record a stable pseudonymous id and keep the real value in run-local state outside the repository. The provenance that matters is 'a PERSON decided this, and which agent acted on it', not which person.

2. digestOf (internal/reconcile/guards.go:404) returns "sha256:" + hex[:32]. That is a sha256 TRUNCATED to 128 bits, still labelled sha256. Two problems: the label is false, and 32 hex characters is exactly the shape of a Cloudflare account id, so every ticfac run record tripped the ticks account detector — 60 findings on one epic. A full digest is 64 hex characters and collides with nothing. Dropping the truncation changes recorded digest values, so decide whether existing evidence keyed by a digest needs a migration or whether a changed digest correctly reads as 'the thing it covers changed'.

Both were worked around on the ticks side for this epic (a narrow guard exemption for sha256-prefixed digest fields, and a placeholder in the decision record). Neither workaround belongs there permanently.
notes: 2026-09-15 14:50 - ticfac run epic-9pd: attempt 5 reported a finding drafted for triage — upstream-tick "Retire the ticks-side workarounds the ticfac settle fix makes obsolete" (key 7436448acfd30d6b7a296f9ae228905d21f6b332270d1362191db758e1acdad5, severity low, for pengelbrecht/ticks). Triage with `ticfac finding 9pd 7436448acfd30d6b7a296f9ae228905d21f6b332270d1362191db758e1acdad5 --promote-as <tick> --by "<who>"` or `--discard --by "<who>"`; the tick cannot close while it is untriaged.
acceptance_criteria: No record ticfac commits to a target repository contains an operator identity handed to a ticfac command; digest fields carry full sha256 values; a test asserts a released_by value does not reproduce the string passed to --release
